as_told.title: Hal Puthoff is open to Wargo's confirmatory-feedback idea

plain: The writer Eric Wargo suggests that remote viewers, people trained in a US government psychic spy programme from the 1970s to the 1990s to describe distant places with their minds, may really be seeing the feedback they will be shown later, when they learn what the target was. Wargo offers this as his own theory. Michels adds that he spoke with Hal Puthoff, whom he calls the founder of the CIA psychic spy programme, and that Puthoff was open to Wargo being right that this later confirmation is needed for remote viewing to work. If so, the mind would be reaching into its own future rather than across space.
